rows: This was a procedural Annual General Meeting (director elections, auditor ratification) with a management financial recap; no shareholder questions were submitted, so there was no Q&A.
CEO John Fieldly framed 2022 as a 'transformational year' with a three-year revenue CAGR of 105%.
Three shareholder-value drivers articulated: revenue growth, operational excellence, and EBITDA growth.
Revenue growth focus: expanding doors and channels - club (entered 2022), food service, college/universities - increasing items per location and driving velocity.

The $194M of distribution-network termination expenses was funded by Pepsi but GAAP-expensed immediately, while the offsetting Pepsi funds are capitalized and amortized over the agreement's life - a timing mismatch; excluding the $194M, FY2022 S&M as a % of sales was consistent YoY.
FY2022 gross margin benefited from lower average can costs (higher-priced international cans working out of inventory), orbit-model freight efficiency, and some pricing benefits.
Q1 2023 gross margin improvement came from lower average can prices and orbit-model leverage, partly offset by higher freight and a few million dollars of inventory write-offs.
Operational-excellence margin levers: orbit-model optimization, direct co-packer-to-distributor shipping, vertical integration, and scrap-waste efficiency.
A days-inventory-outstanding increase at the primary distributor's mixing centers was flagged for Q1 2023 (vs year-end 2022) but not quantified.
Innovation centered on the expanding Vibe line - peach, Arctic, Fantasy, and the newly launched Oasis Vibe (prickly pear lemon), on trend with Gen Z.
Management positions Celsius as a pioneer of better-for-you functional energy and a total-beverage opportunity, not just an energy play.
Global expansion via the Pepsi partnership, Asia strategic partners, and a dedicated Nordics team with a European expansion playbook.
G&A rose on building a scalable back office (employee costs, stock-based compensation, legal/audit/consulting fees).
Voting outcome: all director nominees were elected and Ernst & Young LLP was ratified as independent auditor for the year ending December 31, 2023.

After the management financial recap, VP Business Development Toby David opened the floor for questions via the online portal; no shareholder questions were submitted ('seeing that there have been no questions presented for our review'), so there were no question-answer exchanges. The meeting proceeded directly to the voting results and adjournment.
